svg.title: The station assault from above
svg.desc: Azure defends a fixed station. Ember attacks from the far side. The map is seen from above, with the station at the top and the attackers coming up from the bottom. The azure octagonal station has a chip core and four turret dots inside its hull. A full dashed azure circle shows that its flak reaches about 230 m. Two azure darts below the station are the picket, out from the start. A linked dashed box to the left of the station contains three small azure darts representing the reserve, docked inside. The ember carrier below the circle is on patrol, out of reach. A linked dashed box contains three small craft, including a bomber, representing the rest docked inside. A dashed ember line leads from the carrier's nose up to a tick marked 170 m. Three ember craft with dashed jumping-in arcs point up: a fighter, a bomber and a fighter jump in at speed. Ahead of them, two wide bomber chevrons and short dashed tracks point toward the station. Bombers fire torpedoes from within 240 m, inside the flak. A dashed ember warship beside and ahead of the carrier is the dreadnought, from rules version 10. Two decisions that are not orders are shown below. 1. When the station launches its reserve. The reserve waits docked inside. The scripted commander launches it in the first seconds. A hand rule holds it until the station is hurt. 2. Where the attacker parks its carrier. The scripted commander keeps it on patrol, out of reach. A hand rule brings it in to 170 m once all its craft are out. From rules version 10, the station is the citadel, much bigger, with twelve turrets and four bays. Each turret and bay can be shot off on its own. A dreadnought, a heavy warship, joins the attackers. It waits outside the citadel's reach until the strike goes in.
